name: Stride
lineage: Harlem solo-piano idiom of the 1920s-40s that turned ragtime's written left hand into a virtuoso improvised engine — James P. Johnson's Carolina Shout (1921) as its founding text, extended by Willie The Lion Smith, Fats Waller and Art Tatum — with the left hand leaping a tenth or more between low bass note on beats 1 and 3 and mid-register chord on 2 and 4 at 200-280 BPM, the right hand running broken-octave and arpeggio figures over 32-bar AABB and popular-song forms, and rent-party cutting contests as the training ground.
